statement: The inlier ratio $w$ is the proportion of inliers in the observed dataset, representing the probability of choosing an inlier when a single data point is selected: $w = \frac{\text{number of inliers in data}}{\text{number of points in data}}$.

symbols.meaning: inlier ratio, or the probability of choosing an inlier each time a single data point is selected
minimum number of data points required to estimate model parameters
number of iterations (sample trials) allowed or required in the algorithm
desired probability that the algorithm provides at least one successful result

properties.property: Under independent point selection, the probability that a randomly selected sample subset of $n$ points consists entirely of inliers is $w^n$
properties.why: Each data point in the sample of size $n$ is an inlier independently with probability $w$

properties.property: The probability that at least one of the $n$ selected points is an outlier is $1 - w^n$
properties.why: Complementary event to drawing an all-inlier sample subset of size $n$

properties.property: The number of iterations $k$ required to achieve a desired success probability $p$ satisfies $k = \frac{\log(1-p)}{\log(1-w^n)}$
properties.why: The probability that all $k$ iterations fail to draw an all-inlier sample is $(1-w^n)^k = 1-p$

properties.property: The standard deviation of the required iteration count $k$ is given by $\operatorname{SD}(k) = \frac{\sqrt{1-w^n}}{w^n}$
properties.why: Defined as the standard deviation of the sampling trials required to achieve success

properties.property: Standard RANSAC usually performs poorly when the inlier ratio is below 50% ($w < 0.5$)
properties.why: The probability of obtaining an all-inlier subset decreases substantially, requiring specialized variants such as Optimal RANSAC for heavily contaminated datasets

assumptions.assumption: Data points are selected independently with replacement when forming model hypotheses
assumptions.breaks_when: Points are sampled without replacement from a small dataset, making each selection alter the remaining inlier proportion

assumptions.assumption: A rough estimate or bound of the inlier ratio $w$ is available prior to execution
assumptions.breaks_when: The level of outlier contamination is completely unknown, precluding a principled determination of the iteration budget $k$

failure_modes.mode: Combinatorial iteration explosion / low success probability
failure_modes.signature: Algorithm requires an impractically large iteration count $k$ or fails to find a valid model within allowed iterations
failure_modes.cause: The inlier ratio $w$ is low (e.g., $w < 0.5$), making $w^n$ exceedingly small and driving $k = \frac{\log(1-p)}{\log(1-w^n)}$ to extreme values

failure_modes.mode: Premature algorithm termination with poor fit
failure_modes.signature: RANSAC exhausts $k$ iterations without sampling an all-inlier subset, returning a null or corrupted model estimate
failure_modes.cause: The actual inlier ratio is substantially lower than the assumed value of $w$ used to calculate the iteration count $k$
